sections.headline:
Technology Leadership.
Cybersecurity.
Governance.
sections.supportingCopy: Frontline helps small businesses and nonprofits plan, secure, govern, and improve their technology environments. We combine experienced technology leadership with cybersecurity, compliance, engineering, and managed services so strategy can move directly into execution.

sections.label: Questions worth asking
sections.title: The conversations that keep getting postponed.

questions.text: Do you have a technology roadmap tied to your business plan and budget?
Who is managing your technology vendors, contracts, renewals, and costs?
Are your IT procedures documented, or does one person simply know how everything works?
Are you prepared for CMMC, NIST, HIPAA, or your next customer security review?
Do you know your highest cybersecurity risks, and who owns remediation?
Are you confident that critical company data is properly protected and recoverable?
Your employees are already using AI. Do you know what tools they are using, and what information they are putting into them?
If a major technology decision had to be made tomorrow, who would you turn to?

sections.closingLine: These are the questions Frontline is built to answer.

sections.label: What we do
sections.title:
Five service areas.
One partner.
sections.aside: Frontline can help identify the problem, develop the strategy, establish governance, and then provide the technical resources required to execute the plan.

sections.label: The Frontline operating model
sections.title:
Assess → Standardize → Secure
→ Govern → Lead
sections.aside: A disciplined path, one stage building on the last. Frontline can enter at any point. Most organizations do not start at the beginning.

sections.label: Strategy backed by execution
sections.title: Strategy does not stop at the recommendation.

children.text: Frontline combines experienced technology leadership with hands-on engineering capability. Our team brings decades of combined experience across MSP operations, cybersecurity, project management, systems engineering, cloud, infrastructure, and modern IT operations.
When a roadmap, assessment, or governance program identifies work that needs to happen, Frontline can help carry that work through.

sections.label: Governance, risk & cybersecurity
sections.leftTitle: Compliance should be a managed process, not an annual emergency.

children.text: Frontline builds governance programs around the way an organization actually operates: documented risk, maintained policies, collected evidence, tracked remediation, and readiness that holds up between audits.

sections.rightTitle: From a finding to a fix.

children.text: Because the same team also works in the environment, a control gap does not stop at a finding. Frontline can identify the gap, plan the remediation, and fix the underlying technical problem.

sections.label: Private AI & AI governance
sections.title: Your employees are already using AI.

children.text: The question is whether the organization knows what tools they are using, what information is being shared, and what controls are in place.

Frontline works across three layers: governed access to commercial AI, practical AI governance, and Frontline Private AI, a distinct architecture for organizations that need greater control over where sensitive information is processed and stored.

sections.label: Where Frontline fits
sections.title:
Too small for a full-time IT executive.
Too dependent on technology to go without one.
sections.aside: An organization does not stop needing technology leadership just because it cannot justify hiring a CIO. These are the situations we are built for, most clients arrive in more than one of them.

useCases.title: Nobody owns technology
useCases.description: Decisions get made by whoever happens to be closest to the problem. There is no roadmap, no budget line, no documentation, and no one whose job it is to think a year ahead. Frontline becomes the person who owns it, and leaves you with a plan you can fund.

useCases.title: You have an MSP, but nobody directing it
useCases.description: Tickets get answered. Nothing gets better. A support vendor handles the day-to-day, but no one on your side sets the priorities, reviews the spend, or holds anyone to a standard. Frontline sits on your side of that table, and can keep your current provider in place.

useCases.title: One person is carrying all of IT
useCases.description: Often capable, usually overloaded, and the only one who knows how anything works. There is no peer to think through decisions with, no documentation behind them, and no coverage when they are out. Frontline gives that person a senior partner and gets what is in their head written down.

useCases.title: A security requirement just landed
useCases.description: A customer sent a security questionnaire. A funder added security terms to a grant. An insurance renewal now asks questions it did not ask last year. Or a board wants to know what the exposure is. Frontline works out what actually applies, what is missing, and what order to fix it in.

useCases.title: The environment grew without a plan
useCases.description: Years of one-off decisions, undocumented systems, aging equipment, and accounts nobody has closed. It works until it doesn't, and nobody is sure what breaks if you change something. Frontline documents it, standardizes it, and makes it supportable.

useCases.title: Your team started using AI on its own
useCases.description: Nobody decided to adopt AI. It arrived anyway, one free account at a time, and company information is already going into tools no one approved. Frontline establishes what is allowed, what is not, and where sensitive information is permitted to go.

sections.label: Who we serve
sections.title: Industries & environments.
sections.note: Frontline's leadership brings decades of experience supporting regulated, operational, professional, and technical environments, most of it with organizations small enough that everyone knows everyone.

sections.label: Start a conversation
sections.title:
Tell us where the business is going.
We'll talk about how technology gets there.
sections.lede: Start with a conversation about where you are today, where the business is headed, and where technology, cybersecurity, or governance may be getting in the way.
